images.title: Add in the same unit
images.purpose: Show the one idea the student practises: cut two bars of the same whole into one common unit, then put the shaded units together in a result bar.
images.composition: Three long bars stacked with wide space between them, left edges aligned: two part bars above one result bar.
images.exact_structure: Three long bars of exactly the same length, left edges aligned, each cut by thin lines into 12 equal cells. Top bar: thicker lines after every 3 cells marking fourths; the first 3 cells filled teal #0072B2. Middle bar: thicker lines after every 2 cells marking sixths; the first 2 cells filled amber #E69F00. Bottom result bar, outlined in reddish purple #CC79A7: cells 1 to 3 filled teal and cells 4 and 5 filled amber, the rest plain. Exactly 3 bars, 12 cells each, 3 teal and 2 amber above, 5 filled below.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any controls, menus or screen elements drawn in the frame
images.takeaway: Recut both wholes into the same unit, then count the shaded units together.
images.description: Three same-length bars in 12 equal cells: 3 teal cells show 1/4 = 3/12, 2 amber cells show 1/6 = 2/12, and the result bar holds 5 of them, 5/12.
images.context: Shown with the doer concept before the student practises. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say why 12 works for both fourths and sixths, then count the cells in the result bar.

image_decisions.why: One clean picture of two bars combining in a common unit sets up the adding practice.
